newsitem.title: JAPAN: Saibu Gas to complete shift to natural gas by 2003.
newsitem.headline: Saibu Gas to complete shift to natural gas by 2003.

text.p: Saibu Gas Co Ltd said on Thursday it plans to finish converting the main content of its city gas from liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to natural gas by 2003.

Saibu Gas, which provides gas to more than one million households in Japan's southernmost major island of Kyushu, has decided to switch to natural gas partly because it is clearer than LPG when burned, a company spokeswoman said.
Natural gas produces no sulphur oxide and less carbon dioxide than LPG, she said.
She said the change is expected to help ease Japan's heavy dependence on the Middle East for its energy needs because natural gas is produced at more diverse locations than LPG.

About 80 percent of Japan's LPG imports came from the Middle East in the 1995/96 fiscal year that ended in March, while the region accounted for less than 10 percent of Japan's liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports.
Saibu Gas, with has a 20-year term contract with Malaysia to supply up to 360,000 tonnes of LNG a year, has finished the conversion for more than half of its customers, she said.

Only 20 percent of Japan's municipal gas suppliers still use LPG for their city gas since major gas firms, such as Tokyo Gas Co Ltd, Osaka Gas Co Ltd and Toho Gas Co Ltd, have switched to natural gas.
